It is supposed to be inverse to the producer fusion case of the unpack operation, and in a way it is. The calculation of where result sizes and offsets is analogous to the calculation of the source size and offsets.

Taking the example from above with the pack [30] into [5x6], and input tile size = 5, one can calculate that the first tile should be going to the positions (0, 0) - (0, 4), the second one to (0,5) - (1,3) etc.

On the inverse case, the producer fusion of unpack can overpropagate its input buffer, i.e. read more elements than it needs to calculate the result tile size = 5. For example, to calculate the second tile of unpack [5x6] to [30], one could read a [2x6]slice of the input from the first two outer dims, unpack that and extract the [5] output from the correct positions.

With the consumer pack op pack [30] into [5x6] , one can calculate the offsets and sizes to allocate a big enough input (and output) buffer, insert the [5]input to the right position on the input buffer, e.g. positions (5-9)for the second case from above with an input buffer of shape [12] and pack that into a [2x6]output with all 5 elements in the right positions. Now at this point, I'm having a hard time understanding how one might construct a valid output for the tiled implementation from here. The unpack case used over-utilized the input buffer, where for the inverse we have an under-utilized output, with no way of getting any consumable [Nx6]slice from the overall output buffer [5x6], no matter where (and I guess how) we insert the result buffer of [2x6] in our hands (although we can use a sequence of insert slice ops to place them into the correct positions in the untiled result buffer, that doesn't give us valid results for the tiled implementation I believe). ## MapScatter Approach

After talking to @MaheshRavishankar today (and maybe @Max191 in the other meeting recently), we have a more robust fix. It may not be performant, but it prevents such error in the future. Maintaining the tile size selection logic is not trivial as there could be other new input patterns, so we need a decent fallback solution.

The idea is about using MapScatter op when the fusion is not happening. We can have a pass that performs early bufferization and converts the pack/unpack/relayout ops to map_scatter ops right after distribution; we fuse the map_scatter into the forall op. The rest compilation remains the same.

We don't apply the pass before distribution because we'd lose the opportunity of transpose optimization. It is hard to recover such information from MapScatter op.

This work is independent of the tile size generator; maybe @Max191 can pick it up, as you are the author of the MapScatter op.

## TileSizesGenerator

For tile size generator, I'm putting a rough idea below; someone can help implement it.

### Goals (i.e., what we want to resolve)

1. Decouple tile sizes selection logics and pipeline lowering logics.
  a. Developers can easily set tile sizes for each level. They don’t need to split the list for parallel loops and reduction loops; they don’t need to fully understand the pipeline lowering flow.
  b. We do not want to spread `splitParallelAndReductionTiles` methods/logics everywhere.
  c. We don’t need to spread setting non vector level scalable flags to false everywhere.
2. Better handling for multi lowering config.
  a. Figure out what dims are shared with root op, and what are not.
  b. Have a priority list about setting tile sizes from the rest of compute ops.
  c. Serialize the lowering_config for all the ops in one shot. I.e., do not set lowering config on root op and reset it after adjustments.
3. Give more hints to ops during tile size selection.
  a. Ops can know how tile sizes will be scaled in advance.

### Proposal Ideas

TileSizesGenerator is a class which holds the following information.

- It collects the total number of iteration domains. Some of the dimensions are shared between all the ops, and some of them are only used by an op.
- It can map each iteration domain of an op to the maintained dimension.
- It does not need to know the information about parallel loops and reduction loops.
- It holds 1-3 (distribution, cache, vector) lists about tile sizes. It can set the scalability flag at vector tile sizes level.
- Each tile size can have a set of callback functions, e.g.,
  - Convolution/Pooling ops require some tile sizes (at vector level) being ones, so they can be decomposed to lower rank op and make vectorization happen.
  - Some tile sizes might need to be aligned with unpack’s inner tile sizes to prevent stack allocation.
  - Some tile sizes should be adjusted with the pack's inner tile sizes. Otherwise they will be larger than expected when doing TileAndFuse.
- Given an op, it is able to generate the corresponding lowering_config and set it to the op. This includes splitting the tile sizes for parallel loops (i.e., fusion) and reduction loops (i.e., tiling only).

The callback functions are driven by existing use cases. They can be something else like Policy or Requirement struct, e.g., multiple_of_value.

This class was designed long time ago, but it is suitable for the case. Because it is mostly a helper for mapping iteration space.
RE map_scattor approach, we'd need https://github.com/iree-org/iree/issues/21135 for tensor-based vectorization. It can happen later, as we need it being functional as the first step.

@hanhanW I'll be glad if you could ping me if/when you're working on this. I'll also be interested to work on it and/or contribute at one point but I don't have the time just now 👍 

Also, I guess getting the TileSizeGenerator or at least as a first step adjusting tile sizes for pack (and possibly unpack) ops would also be useful if you wanted to extend [this PR](https://github.com/iree-org/iree/pull/21234) to non-mmt4d dispatches.

> [@hanhanW](https://github.com/hanhanW) I'll be glad if you could ping me if/when you're working on this. I'll also be interested to work on it and/or contribute at one point but I don't have the time just now 👍

Yes, I'll cc you in the PRs. :)

>

I'm okay with starting with TileSizeGenerator if someone has cycles. If it is not an urgent fix, I'd go with the robust fallback approach since it should only take me like `O(days)`. To me, playing with tile size adjustment could be a pain and tech debt atm, since we might re-write the logic and they are too complicated atm.

There are some issues that I need to triage, e.g., additional stack buffers. And there are other work like vectorization. But I verified that https://github.com/iree-org/iree/pull/21444 fixes the issue.

The unpack op is not vectorized because

(1) The [vector size inference](https://github.com/iree-org/iree/blob/cabe97c8fe65137b4e09b83e902e4cca43a40aa9/compiler/src/iree/compiler/Codegen/Utils/Utils.cpp#L1923-L1955) is not available for ukernels ops, which is doable.
(2) Even we turn on using configured vector sizes in vectorization, because it is an invalid vector input sizes. It should be scaled to unpacked domain, which should be `[16, 16]` in the example.

Thus, the issue is about the shape inference. There might be an issue in lowering config propagation, but it is not the direction we want for now. So I'd prefer not to fix that issue. Instead, we should fix the vector size inference.

The IR can be much simpler. To repro: `iree-opt --pass-pipeline="builtin.module(func.func(iree-codegen-generic-vectorization{enable-vector-masking=true use-configured-vector-sizes=false}))" ~/z.mlir`

I guess regardless of the previous discussion on pack ops maybe having precedence over element-wise ops on root op selection, it would be a better starting point to investigate to what extent the consumer fusion can be improved to handle these cases, since we can also have the pack ops ending up in the same dispatch with other non-element-wise ops.

From @egebeysel :

Hi folks! I apologize for the rather long question in advance and please correct me if I'm misinterpreting something. We were having [some cases](https://github.com/iree-org/iree/issues/20723) where the consumer fusion of the pack ops were not happening, and therefore I was trying to complete the tiling implementation of the pack operation for the consumer fusion case, since it currently only supports if the input tile sizes are divisible by the inner tile sizes, see [here](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/blob/854b9e931703dd1b9d8a2b0fe8da787f9e26058d/mlir/lib/Dialect/Linalg/Transforms/TilingInterfaceImpl.cpp#L780-L796).

It is supposed to be inverse to the producer fusion case of the unpack operation, and in a way it is. The calculation of where result sizes and offsets is analogous to the calculation of the source size and offsets.

Taking the example from above with the pack [30] into [5x6], and input tile size = 5, one can calculate that the first tile should be going to the positions (0, 0) - (0, 4), the second one to (0,5) - (1,3) etc.

On the inverse case, the producer fusion of unpack can overpropagate its input buffer, i.e. read more elements than it needs to calculate the result tile size = 5. For example, to calculate the second tile of unpack [5x6] to [30], one could read a [2x6]slice of the input from the first two outer dims, unpack that and extract the [5] output from the correct positions.

With the consumer pack op pack [30] into [5x6] , one can calculate the offsets and sizes to allocate a big enough input (and output) buffer, insert the [5]input to the right position on the input buffer, e.g. positions (5-9)for the second case from above with an input buffer of shape [12] and pack that into a [2x6]output with all 5 elements in the right positions. Now at this point, I'm having a hard time understanding how one might construct a valid output for the tiled implementation from here. The unpack case used over-utilized the input buffer, where for the inverse we have an under-utilized output, with no way of getting any consumable [Nx6]slice from the overall output buffer [5x6], no matter where (and I guess how) we insert the result buffer of [2x6] in our hands (although we can use a sequence of insert slice ops to place them into the correct positions in the untiled result buffer, that doesn't give us valid results for the tiled implementation I believe). I guess this is a similar situation to fusing pack op as a producer with tiled inner dims like [here](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/blob/854b9e931703dd1b9d8a2b0fe8da787f9e26058d/mlir/lib/Dialect/Linalg/Transforms/TilingInterfaceImpl.cpp#L731-L733).

I feel like I might be missing something fundamental over here, so any pointers would actually be much appreciated.

Also, @qedawkins mentioned that it might not be possible to add support for the fusion for this case with the current state of scf.forall + TilingInterface, were you maybe referring to this limitation or am I misinterpreting something here?

Thanks for digging into this. I now remember more details. I think I might know what’s happening, and it may not be supported. The tile sizes of pack op is defined in unpacked domain, which means that the tile sizes are always scaled to be aligned with inner tile sizes. Hey , sorry I was off for a while  and missed the last comment. I'd be down to discuss the tile size generator idea. I guess this would be even more important once one tries to fuse longer sequences of operations than the current setting. So at least coming up with the requirements and/or ideas and listing them here (or somewhere else in a separate issue) would make sense I believe.

## MapScatter Approach

After talking to @MaheshRavishankar today (and maybe @Max191 in the other meeting recently), we have a more robust fix. It may not be performant, but it prevents such error in the future. Maintaining the tile size selection logic is not trivial as there could be other new input patterns, so we need a decent fallback solution.

The idea is about using MapScatter op when the fusion is not happening. We can have a pass that performs early bufferization and converts the pack/unpack/relayout ops to map_scatter ops right after distribution; we fuse the map_scatter into the forall op. The rest compilation remains the same.

We don't apply the pass before distribution because we'd lose the opportunity of transpose optimization. It is hard to recover such information from MapScatter op.

This work is independent of the tile size generator; maybe @Max191 can pick it up, as you are the author of the MapScatter op.

## TileSizesGenerator

For tile size generator, I'm putting a rough idea below; someone can help implement it.

### Goals (i.e., what we want to resolve)

1. Decouple tile sizes selection logics and pipeline lowering logics.
  a. Developers can easily set tile sizes for each level. They don’t need to split the list for parallel loops and reduction loops; they don’t need to fully understand the pipeline lowering flow.
  b. We do not want to spread `splitParallelAndReductionTiles` methods/logics everywhere.
  c. We don’t need to spread setting non vector level scalable flags to false everywhere.
2. Better handling for multi lowering config.
  a. Figure out what dims are shared with root op, and what are not.
  b. Have a priority list about setting tile sizes from the rest of compute ops.
  c. Serialize the lowering_config for all the ops in one shot. I.e., do not set lowering config on root op and reset it after adjustments.
3. Give more hints to ops during tile size selection.
  a. Ops can know how tile sizes will be scaled in advance.

### Proposal Ideas

TileSizesGenerator is a class which holds the following information.

- It collects the total number of iteration domains. Some of the dimensions are shared between all the ops, and some of them are only used by an op.
- It can map each iteration domain of an op to the maintained dimension.
- It does not need to know the information about parallel loops and reduction loops.
- It holds 1-3 (distribution, cache, vector) lists about tile sizes. It can set the scalability flag at vector tile sizes level.
- Each tile size can have a set of callback functions, e.g.,
  - Convolution/Pooling ops require some tile sizes (at vector level) being ones, so they can be decomposed to lower rank op and make vectorization happen.
  - Some tile sizes might need to be aligned with unpack’s inner tile sizes to prevent stack allocation.
  - Some tile sizes should be adjusted with the pack's inner tile sizes. Otherwise they will be larger than expected when doing TileAndFuse.
- Given an op, it is able to generate the corresponding lowering_config and set it to the op. This includes splitting the tile sizes for parallel loops (i.e., fusion) and reduction loops (i.e., tiling only).

The callback functions are driven by existing use cases. They can be something else like Policy or Requirement struct, e.g., multiple_of_value.

This class was designed long time ago, but it is suitable for the case. Because it is mostly a helper for mapping iteration space.
RE map_scattor approach, we'd need https://github.com/iree-org/iree/issues/21135 for tensor-based vectorization. It can happen later, as we need it being functional as the first step.

@hanhanW I'll be glad if you could ping me if/when you're working on this. I'll also be interested to work on it and/or contribute at one point but I don't have the time just now 👍 

Also, I guess getting the TileSizeGenerator or at least as a first step adjusting tile sizes for pack (and possibly unpack) ops would also be useful if you wanted to extend [this PR](https://github.com/iree-org/iree/pull/21234) to non-mmt4d dispatches.

Yes, I'll cc you in the PRs. :)

I'm okay with starting with TileSizeGenerator if someone has cycles. If it is not an urgent fix, I'd go with the robust fallback approach since it should only take me like `O(days)`. To me, playing with tile size adjustment could be a pain and tech debt atm, since we might re-write the logic and they are too complicated atm.

There are some issues that I need to triage, e.g., additional stack buffers. And there are other work like vectorization. But I verified that https://github.com/iree-org/iree/pull/21444 fixes the issue.

issue.body:
Two major changes:
- Allow failure on `linalg.pack` consumer fusion in distribution, which results in leaving consumer ops outside scf.forall ops. It is fusible only if it is perfect tiling scenario.
- Add `BufferizeDispatchTensorLoadStorePass` and `CombineLayoutTransformationPass` pass right after distribution. It applies early bufferization for bindings and fold relayout ops into MapScatterOp. Furthermore, the MapScatterOP is fused into the scf.forall op.

The approach still creates additional stack buffers because MapScatterOp is not vectorized at tensor level. It requires a few more patches to fix it, which is a separate problem from the scope of the revision. E.g., the vector.scatter op needs to take inputs at tensor level: https://github.com/iree-org/iree/issues/21135

Fixes https://github.com/iree-org/iree/issues/20723
